# SEO-213: Expose a breadcrumb trail on deeply nested pages

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

## Statement

A page more than one level below the site root shows its ancestor path as real links, and any breadcrumb markup describes the same trail the page displays.

## Rationale

The trail is what lets a reader arriving directly on a deep page move up into the section it belongs to, and it gives that page an inbound link from every descendant rather than only from a listing.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "has_router",
    "cms",
    "ecommerce",
    "content_publication"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Derive the trail from the route hierarchy rather than from a hand-written list per page, and emit the markup from the same derived structure so the two cannot disagree. Do not invent an intermediate level that has no page behind it.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Compare the visible breadcrumb links in the response against the marked-up trail and against the route hierarchy for the same page.
- Evidence: `RENDERED_HTML`, `JSON_LD`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: none.

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`
- Frameworks: `any`
- Caution: The cited documentation specifies how to mark up a breadcrumb trail that exists. It does not state that a site must have one, so the requirement to show a trail on deep pages is tier B rather than tier A.
